aiOverview.content: #SKYKING is a 2026 documentary thriller streaming on Hulu that details the 2018 story of Richard "Beebo" Russell, a 28-year-old ground agent who stole a Horizon Air plane from Sea-Tac International Airport. The film features never-before-heard audio and family interviews, examining the 70-minute flight and the mental health struggles that led to the incident.Key Details of #SKYKING (2026):Release Date: The film premiered on Hulu on April 14, 2026.Subject: Focuses on Richard "Beebo" Russell, a quiet, friendly ground service agent who took a $33 million aircraft.Content: Features audio recordings of conversations between Russell and air traffic controllers during the flight, as well as insights from family and friends.Focus: Explores themes of the American working class, mental health, and attempts to correct misconceptions about Russell’s motivations.Production: The documentary is part of ABC News Studios and was highlighted by Good Morning America.Background of the Incident:On August 10, 2018, Russell took an empty Horizon Air Bombardier Q400 turboprop plane from Sea-Tac. He flew it for roughly an hour over the Puget Sound, conducting dramatic maneuvers before crashing on Ketron Island, where he was killed. Key Details of #SKYKING (2026): Release Date: The film premiered on Hulu on April 14, 2026. Subject: Focuses on Richard "Beebo" Russell, a quiet, friendly ground service agent who took a $33 million aircraft. Content: Features audio recordings of conversations between Russell and air traffic controllers during the flight, as well as insights from family and friends. Focus: Explores themes of the American working class, mental health, and attempts to correct misconceptions about Russell’s motivations. Production: The documentary is part of ABC News Studios and was highlighted by Good Morning America. Background of the Incident:On August 10, 2018, Russell took an empty Horizon Air Bombardier Q400 turboprop plane from Sea-Tac. He flew it for roughly an hour over the Puget Sound, conducting dramatic maneuvers before crashing on Ketron Island, where he was killed. He was the only person on board, and no one on the ground was injured. The film aimed to address how Russell was mistakenly linked to white supremacist groups by some, with family stating this did not represent him, according to a Seattle Times interview with the director.
